messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered -> high OOM rate on cluster gpu-prod-5 (service: serving-runtime). 20% 5xxs across node pool; multiple container restarts detected.

alex: saw the spike ~10m ago, started triage. CUDA OOMs in logs, but memory usage shows slow steady growth on kv cache on several pods.

maria: copying last 3 log fragments:
```
2026-03-15T03:15:02Z runtime ERROR cuda out of memory while allocating 134217728 bytes
2026-03-15T03:17:11Z allocator WARN paged-attn: page fragmentation high (used 86% of slab)
2026-03-15T03:18:04Z runtime INFO eviction triggered for kv-cache shard=23 freed=12MB
```

kevin: customers report 503/502 errors for long-context requests (>2048). latency for short requests ok. Seems paged attention hot path only.

jen: @maria can you check per-model traffic? Is it limited to a single model or rollout?

maria: done — looks concentrated on model: /open/llama2-13b-quant-paged-2026. Two busy nodes have >70% of its requests.

alex: immediate plan: 1) cordon/drain the two noisy nodes, 2) scale up dedicated pool by +2 nodes, 3) enable immediate fallback to non-paged model variant for affected route.

ops: I'll start drain for gpu-prod-5-12 and gpu-prod-5-15 now. Draining pod: runtime-llama2-13b-zzz on node gpu-prod-5-12 -> kubectl drain started. ETA ~2m.

incident-bot: on-call handoff - alert acknowledged by alex. PagerDuty incident: PD-#12345.

sre-lead: also add throttling rule for routes >1k tokens to reduce burst. Can we gate by token length?

eng-runtime: quick note — we saw a slow kv-cache slab fragmentation bug in the paged allocator in last stable build. There is a hotfix branch that forces periodic defrag/compaction and limits max slab growth.

kevin: what's the impact if we flip to non-paged fallback? token cost up but latency stable. Customers might see higher cost but fewer 5xxs.

customer-success: we have one paying customer affected (AcmeAnalytics) hitting timeouts. CS notified and doing — they want ETA for remediation.

alex: timeline: immediate mitigation -> fallback routing (non-paged) now; medium term -> apply allocator hotfix + rolling restart; long term -> add slab coalescing + KV refcount compaction.

maria: applying fallback route: changed routing policy for /open/llama2-13b/* to model-variant non-paged (canary) at 100%. Command: `redwood route update --name llm-13b --fallback non-paged --force`

incident-bot: routing change detected by deploy-bot. Canary rollout started at 03:22:14Z.

ops: drain complete for gpu-prod-5-12, pods rescheduled. Starting node reboot on 5-12 to force kernel page table shrink.

eng-runtime: pushing hotfix: `git pr create --branch hotfix/paged-defrag --title "paged allocator defrag"` includes: periodic compaction every 5m, enforce eviction when fragmentation > 70%, and telemetry counters. Need manual rollout to avoid regressions.

jen: can we hot-patch configuration first? e.g., set ENV REDWOOD_PAGED_ATTN_COMPACT_INTERVAL=300 and REDWOOD_PAGED_ATTN_MAX_FRAG=70 on runtime pods.

alex: yes, do config flip first. ops, eng-runtime coordinate patch and rolling restart.

ops: done. Env set via k8s patch on runtime daemonset. Rolling restart in progress: 1/12 restarted.

maria: logs after env flip show compaction activity: `paged-attn compaction: shards_compacted=14 reclaimed=48MB` — fragmentation dropping on restarted pods.

kevin: traffic back to normal on routes that were switched. 5xxs reduced from 20% to ~2% for affected customers. Latency for long requests increased ~15% but stable.

customer-success: told AcmeAnalytics the mitigation and that we expect full recovery in ~15-30m. They acknowledged.

eng-runtime: recommend follow-up PR to add slab coalescing and a background scavenger thread to avoid long-term creep. Also propose metrics: per-shard frag_ratio and live_bytes to be added to console.

alex: documenting handoff for next shift: root cause suspected: paged-attention allocator fragmenting under long-lived high-concurrency long-context workloads, slow leak via incomplete refcount frees. Mitigations applied: routing fallback -> non-paged model, compaction env flip, node drain/reboot, increased pool capacity, scheduled rolling restart with hotfix candidate.

alex: handoff checklist for night oncall: 1) watch frag_ratio in telemetry and alert if >65% on any pod, 2) ensure fallback routing remains enabled for impacted routes, 3) coordinate with eng-runtime for rolling hotfix PR tomorrow morning, 4) notify CS if any customer sees >5% 5xxs.

eng-runtime: will open the PR and run extended perf tests. Tagging @sre-lead for postmortem.

jen: I'll create incident thread in postmortems channel with links to logs, compaction metrics, and a short impact timeline.

incident-bot: Incident PD-#12345 status: mitigated -> actions: monitor for 12h, follow-up postmortem required.

alex: thanks team. moving to watch mode. Please escalate immediately if 5xxs climb back over 5%. :eyes:
